name: Exact quotient-root atlas and ternary state-count carry operator
capabilities: compute the exact state-specific coalescence horizon and high-denominator cutoff

core_law: For n>=1 and r>=1, with H=R_(r+1)(r*n-1) and D=floor(n/(H+1)^r), the quotient-root atlas R_r(floor(n/d)), 1<=d<=n, is the disjoint union of an injective D-state high chart and the forced low interval 1..H-1 plus at most the horizon H. Hence |S|+1=D+H+kappa; with q=floor(H/r) the three-point D-band compresses this to |S|+1=H+q+tau with tau in {0,1,2} selected by two exact thresholds.
hard_boundary: DOMAIN_OPERATOR only. The carrier is the finite positive-denominator quotient-root atlas. Do not generalize to arbitrary floor maps or quotient semigroups, do not infer prime/factoring/Legendre or continuum claims, do not erase the H=0 branch, and do not treat the ternary state-count carry as a universal T5 carry law. No Foundation mutation follows.

name: BRC order-one linear deep-tail multiplier transport
capabilities: exact order-one Pell lower ratio (4m+3h)/(4m+h) for h=1,2

core_law: For h in {1,2}, the order-one Pell pair A=4m+3h, B=4m+h satisfies (m+h)B^2-mA^2=h^3 and A/B<sqrt((m+h)/m). Therefore d=floor(2hJ/(4m+h)) is a lower root increment. If J h^3<=mAB, at most two BRC odd-width corrections recover the exact target root/remainder. Since J<=sqrt(mN) and A,B>=4m, the root-free condition 256m^5>=N h^6 suffices; h=2 yields the common mod-8 tail condition 4m^5>=N.
hard_boundary: This is an exact multiplier-state transport optimization only. It does not reduce a Lehman/Hart-style N^(1/3) factor-search horizon, prove an asymptotic factorization speedup, or imply RSA practicality. The deep-tail threshold is enormous at RSA bit sizes. Finite Python speedups are implementation evidence, not machine-model complexity theorems.

name: BRC stride-8 quotient/remainder jet tail
capabilities: decompose the odd-N mod-8 sparse multiplier stream into five fixed-step residue orbits

core_law: For one fixed source residue class modulo 8, let q_m=floor(2hJ_m/(4m+h)) and rho_m be the exact Euclidean remainder. Consecutive visits differ by 8. Under 4m^5>=N and m>=962h, the smooth third-difference plus source-root phase has magnitude below one, while the floor phase contributes strictly between -4 and 4; hence epsilon=q_(m+8)-3q_m+3q_(m-8)-q_(m-16) lies in [-4,4]. Carrying rho and P=(Delta q+Delta^2 q)(D+32) yields the exact provisional residual S=rho+2h(J'-J)-32q-P, normalized by at most four additions/subtractions of D'=D+32. Five orbits times three samples require fifteen seed divisions; all later quotient states are exact recurrence states.
hard_boundary: This extends t0.brc_linear_deep_tail and composes with t0.brc_square_gap_cascade; it is not a new top-level tool family. The proof controls exact multiplier-state transport only and does not shorten a Lehman/Hart-style search horizon or establish a factorization-complexity improvement. Finite Python benchmarks favor the jet only for sufficiently large integers (around 4096 bits in the committed environment); small-size routing should retain native division. The exact quotient remainder must not be collapsed to quotient-only or a fitted real trend.

name: BRC square-increment finite-difference jet tail
triggers: compose quotient jet with square-gap tables
capabilities: retain exact E=q(2J+q) on each of the five fixed-step mod-8 source orbits
prove the exact third-difference product identity coupling quotient and root jets

core_law: On one stride-8 source orbit let s=nabla q, a=nabla^2 q, t=nabla J, u=nabla^2 J, e=nabla^3 q_new, w=nabla^3 J_new and E=q(2J+q). Then nabla^3 E_new = e(2(J+q+s+a+t+u+w)+e)+2w(q+s+a)+6(su+a(s+t)). The quotient jet gives e in [-4,4] and a in [-2,98]. For J=floor(sqrt(mN)), the common tail 4m^5>=N gives 0<Delta_8^3 sqrt(mN)<=384; floor phase contributes strictly between -4 and 4, hence w lies in the sharp integer interval [-3,387]. Retaining M=su and updating M_new=M+s w+(a+e)u+(a+e)w means every post-seed product has a fixed bounded integer factor.
hard_boundary: This is an exact multiplier-state execution optimization extending t0.brc_quotient_jet_tail; it does not shorten a Lehman/Hart-style multiplier horizon, change factor-search complexity, establish RSA practicality, or create a new top-level BRC family. Finite CPython timings favor the difference jet only for sufficiently large integers (near parity at 4096 bits and favorable at 8192/16384 bits in the committed run); smaller inputs should retain the fresh native product. The exact quotient remainder, root finite differences, energy finite differences, and mixed provenance coordinate must not be collapsed.

name: BRC square-increment scaled cross-coordinate jet
capabilities: bijectively replace the older mixed coordinate M using already-retained quotient/root finite differences
evaluate the exact square-increment third difference as e*(2*(J_new+q_new)-e)+2*w*(q_new-e)+C

core_law: Let s=nabla q, a=nabla^2 q, t=nabla J, u=nabla^2 J, e=nabla^3 q_new, w=nabla^3 J_new and M=s*u. Define C=6*(M+a*(s+t)). Because a,s,t are already retained, M=C/6-a*(s+t), so this is an observer-equivalent coordinate change. At the target point, nabla^3 E_new=e*(2*(J_new+q_new)-e)+2*w*(q_new-e)+C. With a_new=a+e and u_new=u+w, C_new=C+6*s*w+6*e*(s+t)+6*a_new*(2*u_new+a_new). The new multipliers are bounded by the inherited e in [-4,4], w in [-3,387] and a_new in [-2,98] bounds.
hard_boundary: This is a compatible constant-factor execution variant extending t0.brc_square_increment_difference_jet, not a new top-level BRC family. It does not reduce the multiplier search horizon or factorization complexity. Finite CPython reference timings show a modest roughly 2.6%-13.8% gain across the tested 1024..16384-bit cohorts; these timings are environment-dependent and not an asymptotic machine theorem. Exact square-gap residue-state transport and a 2-adic front gate were also tested but not promoted because their end-to-end gain was marginal after the energy jet became the dominant cost.
